questions.q: What does echo second > note.txt do if note.txt already contains "first"?
options: Replaces the content: the file now contains only "second"
questions.explain: > replaces the file without asking. >> adds to the end.

questions.q: What does the | in grep 'checkout 500' logs/access.log | wc -l do?
options: Runs the two commands one after the other, separately
Sends grep's output straight into wc -l, which counts the lines
Saves grep's output to a file called wc
questions.explain: A pipe connects one command's output to the next command's input. You only see the final answer.

questions.q: ls logs /nope > out.txt still shows an error on the screen. Why?
options: > only redirects stdout (the normal output); the error goes to stderr, which still goes to the screen
questions.explain: Use 2> to send errors to a file, or > file 2>&1 to send both to the same file.

questions.q: Which pipeline counts how many requests each customer (column 6) made?
questions.explain: uniq -c only merges equal lines that are next to each other, so sort first.

questions.q: You have counts like "7 asha", "31 ravi", "5 sara". How do you put the biggest first?
questions.explain: -n sorts as numbers, -r reverses (biggest first). Plain sort compares text, so 9 would come before 10.

questions.q: Your long pipeline prints nothing. What's the best way to find the problem?
options: Delete the log file and start again
Remove steps from the end until output appears; the last step you removed is where it goes wrong
questions.explain: Build and debug pipelines one step at a time, looking at the output after each |.

questions.q: (Going deeper) What's the difference between cmd > all.txt 2>&1 and cmd 2>&1 > all.txt?
options: The first puts both outputs in the file; the second leaves the errors on the screen
questions.explain: 2>&1 copies stdout's destination at that moment. Redirect stdout to the file first, then send stderr after it.

questions.q: (Going deeper) false | wc -l has exit code 0. What makes the pipeline report the failure?
questions.explain: Normally a pipeline's exit code is the last command's. With pipefail, any failing command makes the pipeline fail.
